content.title: About
content.content: Potato chips, popped, flavored (4202) are light, crunchy snacks made by puffing thinly sliced potatoes without added oil. After puffing, they are coated with flavor blends that give a variety of taste profiles such as cheese, barbecue, sour cream & onion, and more.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popped chips contain roughly 3–4 times less fat than traditional fried chips.
The puffing technology was developed in the 1960s to create lower‑calorie snack options.
Flavor blends often include natural spices but may also contain artificial flavorings.
In the United States, popular flavors include "Sour Cream & Onion", "Barbecue", and "Cheddar".
Packaging is usually foil‑lined to protect against moisture and preserve crunch.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Because they are puffed rather than fried, these chips have a lower fat content, making them a more moderate choice within a balanced diet.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Potatoes retain some dietary fiber after processing, which supports digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Some B‑vitamins such as B6 and B3 survive the processing and contribute to normal metabolism.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Flavor mixes are often salted; individuals monitoring sodium intake should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Certain flavors may contain dairy, gluten, or soy, which are important to consider for people with food allergies.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite lower fat, the chips are still calorie‑dense due to carbohydrates; overconsumption can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the chips straight from the bag as a snack, sprinkle them over salads for added crunch, or use them as a topping for casseroles and soups. Opt for low‑salt versions when possible.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the chips in the original sealed bag or an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Over time they may lose their crunch, so it is best to consume within 2–3 months after opening.
